assumptions:
- "Aligned pores" means at least 3 pores lying along a common straight line. Two pores alone are not considered a row.
- A pore lies on a line if its centroid is within d_eq/2 of the line. In other words, the line passes through the pore's equivalent sphere.
- Candidate lines are every line through the centroids of a pair of pores. Lines are checked in any 3D direction, not just parallel to an axis or a weld or casting direction.
- Pores on the same line only count as one row if neighbours are close enough. The edge-to-edge gap along the line between adjacent pores must be ≤ 6 × the longer pore's length, which is modelled on ASME practice for aligned indications.
- A pore's extent along the line is approximated as its centroid projection ± feret_max/2.
- The length of a pore is its largest Feret diameter (feret_max_mm).
- "Total length" is read literally: the summed length of all pores that belong to any aligned row in the whole part. A pore in several rows is counted only once. It is not evaluated per row.
- "Total length" sums the pore lengths themselves. It does not include the gaps between pores, so it is not the overall span of a row.
- The limit is inclusive: exactly 2.0 mm is accepted, and a 1e-9 numerical tolerance is applied.
- The criterion applies to the whole part. Zones, part volume, wall thickness, surface distance and sphericity are not used.
- A part with fewer than 3 pores is accepted.
- Coincident pore centroids are not used to define a line.

The criterion does not define "aligned". I used the ASME-style definition: 3 or more pores lying on a straight line with an edge-to-edge gap of 1.5 mm or less between neighbouring pores. Both the minimum of 3 pores and the 1.5 mm gap are my choices, not taken from the criterion.
A pore counts as lying on the line if the line passes within its equivalent radius (d_eq_mm / 2) of its centroid. Candidate lines are drawn through the centroids of pairs of neighbouring pores.
Edge-to-edge gaps are approximated by assuming each pore extends feret_max_mm / 2 from its centroid. Gaps are measured along the line, or as centroid distance when choosing candidate pairs, and are clamped at 0.
The length of each pore is its feret_max_mm.
"Total length" is the sum of the individual pore lengths (feret_max_mm) in an aligned group. It is not the overall span from the first pore to the last, which would include the gaps between them.
The 2.0 mm limit applies to each aligned group separately. The part is rejected if any single group's total length is strictly greater than 2.0 mm. Exactly 2.0 mm is accepted, with a 1e-9 tolerance for floating-point error.
All pores are evaluated regardless of zone, distance to the surface, sphericity or local wall thickness. The zones, nominal_wall_mm, part_volume_mm3, dist_surface_mm and wall_mm fields are not used.
Pores open to the surface (dist_surface_mm = 0) are treated like any other pore.
A part with fewer than 3 pores, or with no aligned groups, is accepted.
A missing feret_max_mm or d_eq_mm is treated as 0. Negative values are clamped to 0.

- The criterion does not define "aligned". I treat pores as aligned when a single straight line passes through all of them. A pore counts as on the line if the line comes within d_eq_mm/2 of its centroid, which means it intersects the pore's equivalent sphere.
- Only straight lines through pairs of pore centroids are tested as candidate alignment lines. This finds most alignments but is not a mathematically exhaustive search over all possible lines.
- An alignment needs at least 3 pores. Any 2 pores trivially lie on a line, so 2 is not enough. This follows the usual "aligned indications" convention (e.g., ASME), but it is a choice; the criterion gives no count.
- The criterion gives no spacing rule. I require adjacent pores along the line to be close: the edge-to-edge gap must not exceed the larger feret_max_mm of the two neighbours. Each pore is taken to extend ±feret_max_mm/2 from its projected centroid along the line. A larger gap splits the line into separate groups.
- "Total length of aligned pores" means the sum of the pores' individual lengths (feret_max_mm). It does not mean the end-to-end span of the group, which would include the gaps.
- feret_max_mm is used as the pore length. It may be measured in a different direction than the alignment line, so this is conservative.
- "Must not exceed 2.0 mm" means a total of exactly 2.0 mm is accepted. A small numerical tolerance (1e-9 mm) is applied.
- The limit applies to each aligned group separately. Totals are not summed across different, unrelated alignments in the part.
- The criterion applies to the whole part. Zones, distance to surface, wall thickness, sphericity and part volume are ignored, because the criterion mentions none of them.
- A part with fewer than 3 pores is accepted.
- Pores with identical centroids are not used to define a candidate line, but they can still be members of a line defined by other pores.
- Missing or empty "pores" is treated as no porosity, so the part is accepted.
